negative_findings.description: No authoritative source located for 'City24' as a Ukrainian utility-payment kiosk / self-service terminal operator despite it being named in the cell definition.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian-language query on iBox/EasyPay/City24 returned nothing on City24; the search assistant explicitly noted no City24 results. It may be a brand of another operator, a defunct network, or a name confusion.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If City24 is a real acceptance network, its absence leaves a gap in the utility-kiosk segment; if it is not, the cell definition should be corrected so downstream runs stop chasing it.

negative_findings.description: Could not identify named vendors/integrators of e-ticket validator hardware in Ukraine from the query terms tried ('Смарт Тікет', 'УКРКАРТ', 'СмартТранзит').
negative_findings.result_summary: Those guessed company names returned no matches. Only municipal buyers surfaced (KP GIOTs as Kyiv E-ticket operator, Kyivpastrans buying validators, Kyiv Metro buying QR readers).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The supply side of the validator/e-ticket market is the commercially interesting half. It must be recovered from Prozorro award records (supplier field) rather than by guessing brand names.

negative_findings.description: iBox Bank's licence was revoked and the bank liquidated (NBU decision, 7 March), after which iBox terminals stopped accepting payments for any services.
negative_findings.result_summary: Reported in search results on the iBox terminal network; the network is described elsewhere as ~6,800 terminals in 200 cities carrying ~2,500 services.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: One of the largest non-bank cash-acceptance networks in the cell may be defunct or restructured. Historical iBox tender/partner data must be treated as stale, and the vacated utility-payment volume is a live demand signal for competitors.

negative_findings.description: Some city e-ticket operator selections were advertised in local newspapers rather than in Prozorro or on specialised e-procurement platforms.
negative_findings.result_summary: Reported in Ukrainian regional coverage of e-ticket implementation; flagged there as a transparency problem.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A meaningful slice of municipal payments demand is structurally invisible to any Prozorro-only collection strategy. Regional press monitoring is not optional for this cell — it is the only channel.

negative_findings.description: No Ukrainian-language source found announcing acquiring/POS-terminal tenders run by fuel-retail networks (OKKO, WOG, SOCAR, UPG) or large grocery chains.
negative_findings.result_summary: The АЗС+еквайринг query returned only fuel-price news, network rankings, and generic explainers on what acquiring is; no procurement announcements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Private-sector acceptance procurement in Ukraine appears to run through bilateral negotiation, not published tenders. This segment likely needs an indirect method (partner announcements, association news, terminal-branding observation) rather than tender monitoring.

negative_findings.description: PSP corporate newsrooms (Fondy, WayForPay, LiqPay/Privat, Portmone, EasyPay) were not individually fetched in this pass; only aggregator and comparison coverage of them was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Their existence is well attested across multiple independent guides, but exact newsroom/press-release URLs are unconfirmed and the Fondy domain above is inferred, not verified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: PSP partner and vendor selections are announced on their own channels first. These need a dedicated enumeration pass to pin down per-company news feed URLs.

coverage_gaps.description: No per-company newsroom URLs captured for the core PSP/acquirer set (Fondy, WayForPay, LiqPay, Portmone, EasyPay, Interkassa, Platon, 4bill, PROSTIR-linked providers).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated enumeration pass: for each name in the NBU Payment Infrastructure Register and the EMA member list, resolve the official domain and its press/blog/RSS endpoint.

coverage_gaps.description: The specific ДК021:2015 (CPV) codes under which validators, ticketing systems, parking terminals, self-service kiosks and payment-acceptance services are classified were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Use the Prozorro Infobox CPV documentation and tender.uub.com.ua's DK021 browse to build an explicit code list, then drive the Prozorro API by code rather than by keyword — this is the whole point of the cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Municipal e-ticket coverage captured for Kyiv, Lviv, Kharkiv and Ivano-Frankivsk/Khmelnytskyi only. Dnipro, Odesa, Vinnytsia, Zaporizhzhia, Ternopil, Chernivtsi, Poltava, Zhytomyr and Rivne schemes are uncovered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate oblast-centre transport departments and municipal transport enterprises, capture each scheme's brand name and operator, and register each buyer's EDRPOU for Prozorro tracking.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-newspaper and city-council-bulletin channels — the documented route for some e-ticket operator selections — have no identified aggregator.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate whether city council decision registers (рішення виконкому / оголошення конкурсу) are published online per city, and whether any national aggregator indexes them.

coverage_gaps.description: No official state registry source captured for company identity resolution (EDR / data.gov.ua) — only a commercial mirror (ua-region).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate the official Ministry of Justice EDR open dataset on data.gov.ua and assess licensing for bulk EDRPOU joins against Prozorro supplier records.

coverage_gaps.description: E-money issuers and utility-billing aggregators as a distinct segment were not separately mapped; they were only reached via the NBU register in the abstract.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull the e-money issuer section of the NBU Payment Infrastructure Register explicitly and treat each issuer as a tracked actor.

brief: Payments-ecosystem demand outside Ukrainian banks splits cleanly into a highly documented public half and a nearly undocumented private half. The public half — municipal e-ticketing (Kyiv's KP GIOTs/Kyivpastrans, Lviv's LeoCard, Kharkiv's KharkivPass), parking (KP Kyivtransparkservice) and utility kiosks — is fully visible through Prozorro's open API, BI Prozorro analytics and DoZorro's investigative layer, but only if queries are driven by ДК021/CPV transport and IT codes rather than banking keywords; the CPV list is the single highest-value missing artefact. The private half — PSPs, acquirers, fuel and retail chains — publishes almost nothing tender-shaped, so it must be tracked through the NBU Payment Infrastructure Register as the authoritative actor list, EMA and UAFIC membership rosters, and trade press (psm7.com) partner announcements. Two structural warnings: some city e-ticket operator selections were awarded via local-newspaper notices entirely outside Prozorro, and the iBox terminal network appears to have collapsed with its bank's licence revocation, so historical kiosk data is stale.
